# PRD

- **Spec:** `23_patch_divergence_recovery` (id `23`, name `patch_divergence_recovery`)
- **Title:** Patch Divergence Recovery: Reset to Origin, Backup-Ref Visibility, Protection and Cleanup
- **Status:** active
- **Schema version:** 3
- **Created:** 2026-10-01T14:43:42.131229Z
- **Source:** https://github.com/agent-fox-dev/hub/issues/35
- **Intent hash:** `6acf1dec6f0d798d3664e29d1914798165276f6e5e230b3dd113bd316fd38fc8`

## Intent

When the fork is authoritative for patch branches, sync may discard a hub-side branch tip. It saves that tip under `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` first. This spec makes the saved tip usable and keeps it tidy. An operator can see that a tip was replaced and fetch it back. An operator can move a patch branch to the fork's tip on demand, for example after a `diverged` report. Clients cannot overwrite the hub's backup refs by pushing. The refs are removed when the patch they belong to is removed or purged. A workspace that never replaces a branch behaves exactly as before.

## Goals

- `GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id` exists and returns the patch record, plus `replaced_sha` when `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` exists. Today there is no single-patch GET route.
- `POST /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin` moves a patch branch to the fork's current tip regardless of `PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY`. It saves any discarded hub tip first and returns the patch record. `afc patch reset-to-origin <slug> <patch-id>` calls it.
- A branch moved by a reset triggers the same auto-rebuild as a branch moved by sync, so the move is not lost.
- A client cannot create, update or delete a ref under `refs/hub/replaced/` through the hub's git server. Fetching those refs keeps working.
- `afc patch remove` (`DELETE /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id`) removes the patch's backup ref.
- Purging soft-deleted patches removes their backup refs, and a row whose ref cannot be removed is kept for the next purge.
- Every existing response field, patch status and job record shape is kept. Changes are additive.

## Non-goals

This is the fourth of five scopes. The other scopes have their own specs, and nothing below is built here.

- **`fork_patch_sync`** (`20_fork_patch_sync`, written). It owns `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE`, `PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY`, the origin fetch in sync, the patch refresh and writing `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>`. This spec only reads the backup refs, writes one on reset, and removes them.
- **`fork_patch_registration`** (`21_fork_patch_registration`, written). It owns branch resolution at registration and the single-branch fork fetch. This spec reuses that fetch.
- **`fork_push_control`** (`22_fork_push_control`, written). It owns `PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN` and the pre-receive hook. This spec adds one fixed rule at the same interception point, but no new hook mechanism.
- **`patch_authority_docs`**. It owns the restructure of `docs/carry_patch_workflow.md`, `docs/examples/AGENTS_carry_patch.md`, and ADR 01 status and errata. This spec edits the guide's patch-endpoint table only.
- **A scheduler for purging soft-deleted patches.** Nothing calls `PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches` in production today (see Background). This spec makes the purge clean up refs when it runs. It does not decide when it runs.
- **More than one backup per branch.** The latest replacement overwrites the previous one.
- **A restore-from-backup endpoint.** Recovery is `git fetch <hub_url> refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` and a push to the fork. Nothing resets a branch back to the backup.
- **`replaced_sha` on the list endpoint, in `patch-status`, or in the patch object returned by other endpoints.**
- **Listing or deleting backup refs independently of patches.**
- **Merging, rebasing or conflict-resolving on reset.** The branch is moved. Nothing is merged.
- **Changing `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH`, the follow-up logic of `01_rebuild_worktree`, or the rebuild's use of patch refs.**

## Background

**What exists today** (read in the code):

- The patch REST handlers live in `internal/workspace/patch_handlers.go`: `handleAddPatch`, `handleListPatches`, `handleUpdatePatch`, `handleRemovePatch` and `handleRestorePatch`. `RegisterRoutes` in `internal/workspace/routes.go` mounts them. There is no `GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id`. `docs/api.md` and `docs/openapi.yaml` document only `PATCH`, `DELETE` and `POST .../restore` on that path.
- `patchResponse`, `scanPatch`, `getPatch` and `patchSelectColumns` (`internal/workspace/patch_store.go`) render a patch row. `getPatch` does not filter on status, so it also returns soft-deleted rows.
- The `workspace` and `carrypatch` packages do not import each other. Git-dependent behaviour reaches the workspace handlers through hooks. The workspace package defines the hook type (`BranchCheckFunc` in `branch_check_hook.go`, `CarryPatchSyncFunc` in `sync_hook.go`). `carrypatch` implements it and `cmd/af-hub/main.go` registers it.
- `handleRemovePatch` hard-deletes the row (`deletePatchAndCompact`) and emits `hub.patch.delete`. It touches no git state, and it does not check the workspace status.
- `carrypatch.SQLPatchStore.SoftDeletePatch` sets `status='deleted'`, `deleted_at` and a negative position. `PurgeDeletedPatches(ctx, olderThan)` deletes expired rows across all workspaces and returns only a count. `PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches(ctx, store)` applies a hard-coded 7-day cutoff. **Neither is called from production code.** Only `internal/carrypatch/soft_delete_test.go` calls them. Soft-deleted patches are therefore never purged today.
- The git server (`internal/gitserver/handlers.go`) serves `info/refs` for `git-upload-pack` and the fetch itself with the `git` CLI (`uploadpack.go`), which advertises every ref in the trunk. Pushes go through go-git's receive-pack on the trunk. Spec 22 adds a per-ref pre-receive interception to that path.
- `carrypatch.GitRunner` provides `Run`, `IsAncestor`, `HardReset` and `UpdateRef`. `NewGitRunnerFactory()` builds one for `<workspace_root>/<slug>/trunk`.
- Carry-patch handlers serialise on the trunk with `wslock.TryLock(slug)`. A busy lock answers `409` with error type `workspace_busy` and the message `another operation is running on this workspace; retry later`.
- `emitHubAudit(c, audit.HubEvent)` (`internal/workspace/audit_emit.go`) fills the actor from the request's auth info.
- The rebuild enqueue in sync uses `jobqueue.EnqueueParams` with type `rebuild`, key `slug`, group `slug:integration_branch` and `SubmittedBy` set to the caller. A deduplicated enqueue leaves `rebuild_triggered` false.

**What the earlier scopes deliver that this spec uses:**

- Spec 20 writes `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` before a `replace` outcome. It parses `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE`. It provides a compare-and-swap ref-move helper that also resets the working tree when the moved branch is the trunk's checked-out branch. It provides the `PatchStore` methods that write `origin_sync_state`, `origin_sha` and `origin_synced_at`. It defines the `hub.patch.replace` audit event, the origin credential resolver, and the `502` messages `origin fetch failed` (error type `origin_fetch_failed`) and `failed to resolve origin credentials`.
- Spec 21 provides a single-branch fork fetch (`+refs/heads/<name>:refs/remotes/origin/<name>`, no tags, no prune) and its classification of "branch not on origin", separate from other fetch failures.
- Spec 22 provides the interception of ref writes in the git server's receive session, with a per-ref error that reaches the client as `ng <ref> <message>`.

The names of those helpers are fixed by the earlier implementations. This spec refers to them by role.

**Why this scope needs more than the issue lists:**

1. The issue extends `GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id`, but the route does not exist. It is added here.
2. A reset that reads only the existing `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` can use a stale tracking ref. In `hub` mode nothing refreshes it after the clone. The reset therefore fetches that one branch first.
3. A branch moved by a reset looks `in_sync` at the next sync. Without a rebuild trigger of its own, the move would never reach the integration branch until something else changed. Spec 20 has the same reasoning for sync.
4. The purge routine is unwired, so DR-4's "when the row is purged" has no production trigger. This spec makes the routine correct and leaves the schedule to a later decision.
5. Always writing a backup on reset would let a harmless fast-forward overwrite the one backup that holds real discarded work.

## Requirements

### 1. `GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id`

The route is mounted next to the other patch routes and requires `patches:read` (a `patches:write` PAT also passes, as for the list endpoint). Ownership works as for the other patch endpoints: the owner or an admin, and `404 workspace not found` otherwise. An unknown patch id answers `404 patch not found`. A soft-deleted patch is returned with its `deleted` status.

The response is the existing patch object (`patchResponse`, including any `origin_*` fields spec 20 adds). When `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` resolves to a commit, it also carries `replaced_sha`, the full 40-character SHA. The field is omitted when the ref does not exist, when the workspace's trunk is not on disk (for example an archived workspace), when no recovery hook is registered, and when the lookup fails. A lookup failure is logged at warn level and never fails the request. The other patch endpoints are unchanged and do not carry `replaced_sha`.

Verification: tests cover the field present, the field absent without a backup, a soft-deleted patch, an archived workspace, a non-owner (`404`), a PAT without `patches:read` (`403`) and an unknown id.

### 2. `POST /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin`

The endpoint requires `patches:write`. Ownership and the "workspace is not active" and "workspace is not in carry_patch mode" `400` responses work as in `handleRestorePatch`. A workspace whose `clone_status` is not `ready` answers `409` with the message `workspace clone is not ready`.

Preconditions on the patch, checked in this order:

- An unknown id answers `404 patch not found`.
- A patch named like the workspace's integration branch answers `400 patch branch is the integration branch`. The integration branch is never moved by this endpoint.
- A patch with status `merged_upstream` or `deleted` answers `409` with the message `patch status <status> cannot be reset`. Only `active`, `conflict` and `disabled` patches are eligible, matching the candidates of sync.

The endpoint takes the workspace lock with `wslock.TryLock(slug)` and holds it for the whole operation. A busy lock answers `409 workspace_busy` with the message above. It is not taken before the checks above succeed.

The success response is `200` with the patch object as `GET` renders it (including `replaced_sha` when a backup exists after the reset). It also carries `rebuild_triggered` (boolean) and `rebuild_job_id` (string, only when a job was enqueued), the same meaning as in the sync response. The reset works in both `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE` modes and is not limited by `PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY`.

Verification: handler tests cover each status code and message above, with the hook stubbed. Integration tests cover requirement 3.

### 3. Reset semantics

Under the workspace lock, the reset does the following.

1. **Fetch the branch.** It runs the spec 21 single-branch fetch `+refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` with origin credentials from the spec 20 resolver (`GIT_PAT`, then `GIT_USERNAME`/`GIT_PASSWORD`, then none). The fetch runs in both modes, because the operator is asking for the fork's tip now.
   - A credential failure answers `502 failed to resolve origin credentials`.
   - A fetch failure answers `502 origin fetch failed` with error type `origin_fetch_failed`.
   - A branch the fork does not have answers `409` with error type `missing_on_origin` and the message `branch does not exist on origin`.
   - Error text from the fetch is logged and is not echoed.
   - In all three cases nothing is written.
2. **Resolve both tips to SHAs.** The fork tip is `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>^{commit}`. The local tip is `refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}`, and may be absent.
3. **Apply the first matching rule.**
   - *Local branch missing.* Create `refs/heads/<branch>` at the fork tip with a compare-and-swap create. Action `created`. No backup is written.
   - *Same commit.* Write nothing. Action `none`. The response is still `200`.
   - *The local tip is a strict ancestor of the fork tip* (a fast-forward). Move the local branch. Action `fast_forwarded`. No backup is written, because no commit is discarded.
   - *Anything else* (diverged, or the fork tip is a strict ancestor of the local tip). First write the local tip to `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>`, overwriting any earlier backup. Then move the local branch. Action `replaced`.

   Ancestry uses `GitRunner.IsAncestor` on SHAs. The move reuses spec 20's compare-and-swap helper: `update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>`, with `update-ref` and never `checkout`, `reset` or `branch -f`, and a hard reset of the working tree when the moved branch is the trunk's checked-out branch. If spec 20's implementation does not expose that helper in a form `carrypatch` can call from here, it is extracted and shared, not duplicated.
4. **Lost race.** A hub push can land between the SHA resolution and the write. If the compare-and-swap fails, the endpoint answers `409` with error type `ref_changed` and the message `patch branch changed during reset; retry`. A backup already written stays. It points at the tip the branch had when it was read, and a retry overwrites it. Any other write failure answers `500 failed to update patch branch <branch>`.
5. **Persisted sync state.** When `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE` is `origin`, a reset that completes (any action) records the patch's state through spec 20's `PatchStore` method as `in_sync`, with `origin_sha` set to the fork tip and `origin_synced_at` set to now. The dashboard then no longer shows `diverged` for the patch. When the source is `hub`, nothing is written, because spec 20 clears that state at each hub-mode sync.
6. **Rebuild.** When the branch moved (action `created`, `fast_forwarded` or `replaced`) and the patch status is `active` or `conflict`, the endpoint enqueues a `rebuild` job exactly as sync does: same type, key, group, payload builder and deduplication, with `SubmittedBy` set to the caller. It does so unless `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC` is `"false"`. A moved `disabled` patch does not trigger a rebuild, because the rebuild skips it. A deduplicated enqueue leaves `rebuild_triggered` false. An enqueue error is logged and does not fail the reset.

Verification: integration tests with a real bare fork and a real trunk, asserting the local ref, the backup ref, the response, the persisted state and the rebuild for each rule. They also cover:
- the trunk's checked-out branch being moved and the working tree following;
- a fast-forward not touching an existing backup;
- a repeated `replaced` reset overwriting the backup;
- the three `502` and `409` paths leaving every ref unchanged;
- a hub push racing the move (`ref_changed`);
- `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC=false` suppressing the rebuild;
- a `disabled` patch not triggering a rebuild;
- a reset in `hub` mode writing no persisted state.

### 4. CLI: `afc patch reset-to-origin`

`afc patch reset-to-origin <workspace-slug> <patch-id>` takes exactly two arguments, sends `POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/patches/<id>/reset-to-origin` with no body, and prints the JSON result. It is added to `PatchCmd` in `internal/cli/patch_cmd.go`, with the same `SilenceErrors`/`SilenceUsage` and `apikit.CLIHandleError` handling as `patch restore`. Its help text names the backup ref and the `replaced_sha` field.

Verification: a CLI test with a stub server covers the path, the method, the printed result and error propagation.

### 5. Protecting `refs/hub/replaced/*` in the git server

The git server never accepts a client push that creates, updates or deletes a ref whose name starts with `refs/hub/replaced/`. The rule is built into `internal/gitserver`. It applies to every workspace and every credential with `git:write`, and it does not depend on a registered pre-receive hook or on the workspace mode.

It is evaluated at the spec 22 interception point, before the registered pre-receive hook is consulted, so the rejection is a per-ref status. The client sees `unpack ok` and `ng <ref> refs/hub/replaced/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to`. Other refs in the same push are processed as usual. The rejected ref keeps its old value. Because spec 22's accepted-refs-only rule applies, a rejected ref triggers no `head_sha` update, no audit entry and no post-push hook.

Hub-internal writes (sync, reset, removal) do not pass through a client push and are unaffected. Other names under `refs/hub/` are not covered by this rule. Spec 22 is the only other user of that namespace (`refs/hub/forward/`), and it removes its own temporary refs.

Fetching is unchanged. The `git` CLI serves `git-upload-pack` and advertises every trunk ref, so `git ls-remote` and `git fetch <hub_url> refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` already work. A test asserts this, so a later change to the advertisement cannot silently break recovery.

Verification: gitserver tests with a real `git push` cover:
- a rejected create, update and delete;
- a push mixing a `refs/hub/replaced/` ref with a normal branch, where the branch is written and only the protected ref is rejected;
- a standard-mode workspace getting the same rejection;
- a client fetching a backup ref by name;
- the backup ref being listed by `ls-remote`.

### 6. Backup cleanup on `afc patch remove`

After `deletePatchAndCompact` succeeds in `handleRemovePatch`, the handler asks the recovery hook to delete `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` for the removed patch (`git update-ref -d`). Removal is best effort.

- A missing ref counts as success.
- A missing trunk, as for an archived workspace, counts as success and is logged at info level.
- Any other failure is logged at warn level with slug, branch and error. It never changes the response: `204` is still returned, because the row is already gone.
- No workspace lock is taken. Deleting a single ref is atomic in git, and taking the lock would make `DELETE` start failing with `409` during a sync.

The patch row is looked up before deletion (`handleRemovePatch` already does so for the audit event), and the branch name is taken from that lookup. Without a registered hook, nothing is removed and removal works as today. Soft deletion by a rebuild does not remove the ref, so `POST .../restore` brings back a patch with its backup intact.

Verification: tests cover removal with and without a backup, a trunk that is missing, a failing hook still returning `204`, and soft-delete plus restore keeping the ref.

### 7. Backup cleanup on purge

Purging expired soft-deleted patches removes each purged patch's backup ref.

- The `PatchStore` interface gains a method that lists the soft-deleted rows older than a cutoff, with id, workspace slug and branch name. `SQLPatchStore` and the test doubles implement it.
- The purge routine, for each expired row, removes `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` in that workspace's trunk. It then deletes that row (by id, only while `status='deleted'`). A row whose ref removal failed is left in place and retried at the next purge, with a warn log. A missing ref or a missing trunk counts as success.
- The routine returns the number of rows purged. `PurgeDeletedPatches` keeps its current signature and behaviour for existing callers.
- The routine takes the workspace root and the same git runner factory the other carry-patch code uses. The existing two-argument `PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches(ctx, store)` keeps working without ref cleanup. The ref-aware variant is a new function with the same 7-day retention.
- No scheduler is added and no call is wired into `cmd/af-hub/main.go`.

Verification: tests cover purge with and without a backup ref, a failing ref removal keeping the row, a missing trunk purging the row, and rows within the retention window being untouched.

### 8. Package boundaries and wiring

The workspace package defines a recovery hook type in a new file next to `branch_check_hook.go`, with a registration function and a nil default. It carries three operations:

- reading the replaced SHA for a slug and branch;
- removing the backup ref for a slug and branch;
- running a reset for a slug, a patch and the calling auth info, returning the action, the SHAs and the rebuild outcome, or a classified error.

The classified errors distinguish: workspace busy, branch missing on origin, origin fetch failure, credential failure, ref changed, and other failure. The handlers map them to the status codes and messages of requirement 3.

`internal/carrypatch` implements the hook with the git runner factory, the workspace root, the variable getter (`store.GetVariableValue`), the origin credential resolver, the single-branch fetch function (injectable, so tests can use a stub), the job queue, the spec 20 `PatchStore` methods and the `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE` parser. `cmd/af-hub/main.go` registers it next to the existing hooks. The workspace package does not import `carrypatch`, and `carrypatch` does not import `workspace`.

If the hook is not registered, `GET` omits `replaced_sha`, `DELETE` skips the cleanup, and the reset endpoint answers `500` with the message `patch reset is not configured`.

The route handlers use the existing workspace auth helpers (`requirePatchReadScope`, `requirePatchWriteScope`, `lookupPatchWorkspace`) built on `apikit.GetAuthInfo`, per the project steering. No local auth structs or custom context keys are added.

### 9. Audit and logging

A successful reset emits one `hub.patch.reset` event with `resource_type` `patch`, the workspace slug, the caller as actor, and metadata `{ branch_name, action, local_sha, origin_sha, replaced_sha }`. `action` is one of `none`, `created`, `fast_forwarded` or `replaced`. `local_sha` is the tip before the reset and is omitted when there was no local branch. `replaced_sha` is present only for `replaced`. The event type is added as a constant in `internal/audit/types.go` next to `EventRebuildFollowup`.

A reset with action `replaced` also emits `hub.patch.replace`, the event spec 20 defines for sync replacements, with `branch_name`, `replaced_sha`, `origin_sha` and an added `trigger` key set to `reset_to_origin`. Events emitted by sync carry no `trigger` key, and a consumer reads its absence as `sync`.

A failed reset emits nothing. Replacements and removals are logged at info level with slug, branch and the SHAs. A nil emitter skips emission, and an emit error is logged without affecting the response.

Verification: tests assert the event types and metadata for each action, the absence of events on failure, and a failing emitter not changing the outcome.

All of the following are updated in the same change, per the project steering.

- **`docs/api.md`:**

- **`docs/cli.md`:** `afc patch reset-to-origin`.

- `docs/configuration.md` is unchanged, because this spec adds no variable or environment key.

## Design Decisions

1. **The single-patch GET route is added here.** The issue says to extend it, but it does not exist in `RegisterRoutes`, `docs/api.md` or the OpenAPI file. A `replaced_sha` field needs a read endpoint, and the route is small. It returns the existing patch object, so nothing else changes.
2. **`replaced_sha` appears on the single-patch GET only.** Reading a ref per row on the list endpoint would add a git call to every list request. The issue asks for the single-patch endpoint, and an operator looking at a `replaced` outcome already has the patch id.
3. **The reset and the removal hook sit behind a hook in the `workspace` package.** `patchResponse`, the auth helpers and `emitHubAudit` live in `workspace`, and git and the lock live in `carrypatch`. The two packages cannot import each other, and the existing sync and branch-check hooks solve the same split the same way.
4. **The reset fetches the one branch before moving it.** The issue says to move to `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`. In `hub` mode that ref is as old as the clone, and in `origin` mode it is as old as the last sync. Resetting to it could move a patch to a stale tip and look like a success. The single-branch fetch from spec 21 is already available. The cost is a possible `502`, which is clearer than silent staleness.
5. **The reset writes a backup only when it discards commits.** The issue says to write the backup "first as in PB-5", and PB-5 is the diverged case. With one backup per branch, an unconditional write would let a fast-forward overwrite a backup that still holds real discarded work. A `replaced_sha` therefore always means that a tip was discarded.
6. **The reset enqueues a rebuild like sync does.** The issue says the endpoint returns the patch record. A branch moved by the reset reads `in_sync` at the next sync, so no later event would pick it up, which is the reasoning of spec 20's decision on ref-write failures. The trigger uses `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC`, the same opt-out as a fork-driven move. The response gains `rebuild_triggered` and `rebuild_job_id` as additive fields.
7. **Only `active`, `conflict` and `disabled` patches can be reset.** These are the statuses sync refreshes. A `merged_upstream` or `deleted` patch is no longer part of the rebuild, and moving its branch would only confuse the dashboard.
8. **A reset updates persisted sync state only in `origin` mode.** Spec 20 clears that state at every hub-mode sync and shows it only for workspaces that opted in. Writing it in `hub` mode would show a state that disappears at the next sync.
9. **The `refs/hub/replaced/` rule is built into the git server and independent of workspace mode.** The reserved ref is written only by the hub. A fixed rule needs no database lookup and cannot fail open on a query error. A rule inside the carry-patch hook would leave standard workspaces and a missing hook unprotected. It reuses spec 22's interception point rather than adding a mechanism.
10. **The protected prefix is `refs/hub/replaced/`, not all of `refs/hub/`.** That is what the issue names. Spec 22 keeps a temporary ref under `refs/hub/forward/`, and a broader rule could collide with the way it writes that ref.
11. **`DELETE` removes the backup ref on a best-effort basis and takes no lock.** The row is already gone, so a failed ref removal must not turn a completed delete into an error. Taking the workspace lock would make `DELETE` return `409` during a sync, which it does not today.
12. **Purge keeps a row until its ref has been removed.** Removing the row first would orphan the ref, and nothing else would ever find it. Leaving the row means the next purge retries, at the cost of an expired row living a little longer after a git failure.
13. **The purge routine is made correct, but not scheduled.** `PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches` has no production caller. Scheduling it would start permanently deleting rows that have never been deleted, which is a data-retention decision outside this scope. It is recorded as an open question.
14. **Errors on the reset use `409` for states, `502` for the fork and `500` for the hub's own failures.** A missing fork branch, a lost race and a busy workspace are conditions of the resource. A failure to reach the fork is an upstream failure, with the messages and error type already fixed by specs 20 and 21. Typed errors let scripts branch without matching text.
15. **The reset has its own `hub.patch.reset` event, and a replacement also emits `hub.patch.replace`.** Operators filter on `hub.patch.replace` to find every discarded commit, and sync emits it for the same reason. A `trigger` key tells the two sources apart, and its absence means sync, so spec 20's events do not change.
16. **No new CLI flags and no `--force`.** The endpoint is explicit by its name and already ignores the divergence policy. A confirmation flag would only duplicate the command's meaning.

## Dependencies

| Spec | Relationship | Why |
|------|--------------|-----|
| `20_fork_patch_sync` | depends | It writes `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` and defines `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE` parsing, the compare-and-swap ref-move helper, the `PatchStore` methods for `origin_*` state, the origin credential resolver, the `502` messages and the `hub.patch.replace` event. This spec reads and removes the backup refs and reuses all of those. |
| `21_fork_patch_registration` | depends | The reset reuses its single-branch fork fetch and its "branch not on origin" classification, and follows its hook pattern between `workspace` and `carrypatch`. |
| `22_fork_push_control` | depends | The `refs/hub/replaced/` rejection is added at the receive-pack interception point and per-ref status path that spec introduces, and relies on its accepted-refs-only rule. |
| `01_rebuild_worktree` | depends | The rebuild enqueued by a reset is the job that spec's executor runs. Its snapshot and follow-up logic is unchanged. |
| `15_carry_patch_workspace` (archived) | modifies | The patch REST handlers and routes gain a `GET` by id and the reset endpoint. Patch removal gains the cleanup call. |
| `16_carry_patch_operations` (archived) | modifies | `PatchStore` gains the expired-patch listing, and the purge routine gains a ref-cleaning variant. |
| `06_git_server` (archived) | modifies | Receive-pack gains the fixed protected-namespace rule. |
| `18_hub_audit_query` (archived) | modifies | New hub event type `hub.patch.reset`, and an added `trigger` key on `hub.patch.replace`. |
| `09_git_credentials` (archived) | depends | `ResolveCloneAuth` for the fork credentials used by the reset's fetch. |

## Verified External API

No new external module is used. `github.com/go-git/go-git/v5` v5.19.1 (go.mod) is used only indirectly, through the fetch from spec 21 and the receive-pack path of spec 22. Its source is outside the repository and could not be read.

Git CLI commands run through `GitRunner.Run`. Their behaviour is standard git, and is exercised by the integration tests:

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `git update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>` | Compare-and-swap move. An all-zero old value means "must not exist". |
| `git update-ref <ref> <sha>` (`GitRunner.UpdateRef`) | Force-write the backup ref. |
| `git update-ref -d <ref>` | Delete a backup ref. Exit 0 when the ref is absent. **Unverified** for the repo's git versions. The test for a missing ref confirms it. |
| `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}` | Resolve a tip. A non-zero exit means the ref is absent. |
| `git merge-base --is-ancestor` (`GitRunner.IsAncestor`) | Ancestry on SHAs, with the exit-code discrimination in `internal/gitcmd/ancestor.go`. |

Repository symbols this spec calls, read in this repo: `carrypatch.GitRunner.{Run, IsAncestor, UpdateRef, HardReset}`, `carrypatch.NewGitRunnerFactory`, `carrypatch.PatchStore`, `carrypatch.SQLPatchStore.{SoftDeletePatch, PurgeDeletedPatches}`, `carrypatch.PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches`, `carrypatch.BuildRebuildPayload`, `workspace.patchResponse`, `workspace.getPatch`, `workspace.requirePatchReadScope`, `workspace.requirePatchWriteScope`, `workspace.lookupPatchWorkspace`, `workspace.emitHubAudit`, `workspace.ResolveCloneAuth(store *secrets.Store, slug string) (transport.AuthMethod, error)`, `wslock.TryLock(slug) (unlock func(), ok bool)`, `jobqueue.EnqueueParams`, `apikit.GetAuthInfo`, `apikit.WriteAPIError`, `apikit.WriteAPIErrorWithType`, `apikit.CLIHandleError` and `apikit.CLIClientFromCmd`.

The following come from specs 20, 21 and 22. They are not yet in the code, and their names are fixed by those specs' implementations:

- the `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE` parser;
- the origin credential resolver;
- the compare-and-swap ref-move helper;
- the `PatchStore` methods that write origin sync state;
- the single-branch fork fetch and its classification of a missing branch;
- the receive-pack interception point.

Treat all of them as **unverified**. If a helper is not reachable from `carrypatch` (for example, it sits in a test-only file or is unexported in another package), the implementation extracts it instead of duplicating it.

## Glossary

- **PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE**: Workspace variable defined by spec 20 with the modes hub and origin.
- **backup ref**: The hub-side ref refs/hub/replaced/<branch> that holds the last hub branch tip discarded when a patch branch was moved to the fork's tip.
- **compare-and-swap move**: A git update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old> call that fails if the ref no longer holds the expected old value; supplied by spec 20.
- **fork**: The origin repository of a carry_patch workspace, from which the trunk was cloned.
- **protected namespace**: Ref names beginning with refs/hub/replaced/, which the git server never lets a client create, update or delete.
- **recovery hook**: The hook type defined in the workspace package, with a nil default, through which carrypatch supplies backup-ref reading, backup-ref removal and reset. It exists because workspace and carrypatch do not import each other.
- **replaced_sha**: The full 40-character SHA that a backup ref resolves to, returned by GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id when the ref exists.
- **reset action**: One of none, created, fast_forwarded or replaced: the outcome a reset-to-origin reports.
- **reset-to-origin**: The operator-initiated move of a patch branch to the fork's current tip, regardless of PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY.
- **trunk**: The hub's on-disk git repository for a workspace at <workspace_root>/<slug>/trunk.
- **workspace lock**: The per-slug lock taken with wslock.TryLock(slug) that serialises operations on a trunk.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id

**Rationale:** An operator who sees a replaced outcome needs a read endpoint that shows whether a recoverable backup tip exists.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN an owner, an admin or a PAT holding patches:read or patches:write sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id for an existing patch and refs/hub/replaced/<branch> resolves to a commit in the workspace trunk, THE workspace handler SHALL return the existing patch object (patchResponse, including any origin_* fields) plus replaced_sha holding the full 40-character commit SHA
   → HTTP 200 with the patch object and a replaced_sha string of 40 hexadecimal characters
   Check: unit
   - setup: an owned carry_patch workspace with one patch
   - setup: a stub recovery hook whose ReadReplacedSHA returns a 40-hex SHA for the patch branch
   ```
   for caller in [owner, admin, pat_read, pat_write]: r = get(path, caller); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.replaced_sha == SHA; assert re.match('^[0-9a-f]{40}$', r.json.replaced_sha); assert r.json.id == patch.id
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN the patch is requested and the backup ref does not exist, or the workspace trunk is not on disk, or no recovery hook is registered, THE workspace handler SHALL return the patch object without a replaced_sha key
   → HTTP 200 with the patch object; the JSON body contains no replaced_sha key
   Check: unit
   - setup: an owned carry_patch workspace with one patch
   ```
   for setup in [no_ref_hook, no_trunk_hook, nil_hook]: r = get(path); assert r.status == 200; assert 'replaced_sha' not in r.json
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF the recovery hook returns an error while reading the backup ref, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL log the failure at warn level and return the patch object without replaced_sha
   → HTTP 200 with the patch object, no replaced_sha key, and one warn-level log entry
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hook whose ReadReplacedSHA returns an error
   - setup: a captured log handler
   ```
   r = get(path); assert r.status == 200; assert 'replaced_sha' not in r.json; assert count(logs, level=WARN) == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN the requested patch has status deleted, THE workspace handler SHALL return the patch object with its deleted status
   → HTTP 200 with status "deleted"
   Check: unit
   - setup: a patch with status deleted and a non-empty deleted_at
   ```
   r = get(path); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.status == 'deleted'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF the patch id does not exist in the workspace, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the request
   → HTTP 404 with error message "patch not found"
   Check: unit
   - setup: an owned workspace with no patch of the requested id
   ```
   r = get('/patches/999999'); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.message == 'patch not found'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] IF the caller is neither the workspace owner nor an admin, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the request without revealing the workspace
   → HTTP 404 with error message "workspace not found"
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace owned by user A and a patch in it
   - setup: an authenticated user B who is not an admin
   ```
   r = get(path, as_user_b); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.message == 'workspace not found'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] IF the caller is a PAT that holds neither patches:read nor patches:write, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the request
   → HTTP 403
   Check: unit
   - setup: a PAT whose permissions are ["workspaces:read"] only
   - setup: an owned workspace with a patch
   ```
   r = get(path, pat(['workspaces:read'])); assert r.status == 403
   ```
1. [REQ-1.8] THE workspace handler SHALL for any other patch endpoint (list, add, update, remove, restore, sync), return a patch object without a replaced_sha key
   → no patch object in any response body contains a replaced_sha key
   Check: property
   - setup: a stub hook that always returns a backup SHA
   ```
   for ep in [list, add, update, restore, sync]: body = call(ep, gen_patch_state()); for p in patch_objects(body): assert 'replaced_sha' not in p
   ```

### REQ-2: POST /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin: authorization, preconditions and locking

**Rationale:** A reset moves a branch, so it must refuse every state in which moving is wrong before it takes the lock or touches git.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN an authorised caller sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin for an eligible patch and the reset completes, THE workspace handler SHALL return the patch object as GET renders it (including replaced_sha when a backup exists after the reset) plus rebuild_triggered and, only when a job was enqueued, rebuild_job_id
   → HTTP 200 with the patch object, rebuild_triggered (boolean) and optional rebuild_job_id (string)
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hook whose RunReset returns action replaced, SHAs, rebuild_triggered true and job id "job-1" and whose ReadReplacedSHA returns a SHA
   - setup: an eligible active patch
   ```
   r = post(path); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.rebuild_triggered == True; assert r.json.rebuild_job_id == 'job-1'; assert r.json.replaced_sha == SHA
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF the caller is a PAT without patches:write, or is neither the owner nor an admin, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the request before any git operation
   → HTTP 403 for a PAT without patches:write; HTTP 404 with message "workspace not found" for a non-owner non-admin
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hook counting RunReset calls
   ```
   assert post(path, pat(['patches:read'])).status == 403; r = post(path, other_user); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.message == 'workspace not found'; assert hook.calls == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF the workspace is not active or is not in carry_patch mode, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the request with the same 400 messages as handleRestorePatch
   → HTTP 400 with the "workspace is not active" or "workspace is not in carry_patch mode" message
   Check: unit
   - setup: one archived workspace and one standard-mode workspace, each with a patch id
   ```
   assert post(archived).status == 400 and msg == 'workspace is not active'; assert post(standard).status == 400 and msg == 'workspace is not in carry_patch mode'
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF the workspace clone_status is not ready, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the request
   → HTTP 409 with message "workspace clone is not ready"
   Check: unit
   - setup: an active carry_patch workspace with clone_status "cloning"
   ```
   r = post(path); assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.message == 'workspace clone is not ready'; assert hook.calls == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF the patch id is unknown, or the patch branch name equals the workspace integration branch, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the request in that order and never move the integration branch
   → HTTP 404 with message "patch not found" for an unknown id; HTTP 400 with message "patch branch is the integration branch" for the integration branch
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace with integration branch "main"
   - setup: a patch whose branch_name is "main"
   ```
   assert (post(unknown).status, msg) == (404, 'patch not found'); assert (post(main_patch).status, msg) == (400, 'patch branch is the integration branch'); assert hook.calls == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] IF the patch status is merged_upstream or deleted, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the request; only active, conflict and disabled patches are eligible
   → HTTP 409 with message "patch status <status> cannot be reset"
   Check: unit
   - setup: one patch with status merged_upstream and one with status deleted
   ```
   for s in ['merged_upstream','deleted']: r = post(patch_with(s)); assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.message == f'patch status {s} cannot be reset'
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] IF wslock.TryLock(slug) reports the workspace is busy after the preceding checks passed, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the request without writing any ref; the lock is taken only after the checks succeed and is held for the whole operation
   → HTTP 409 with error type workspace_busy and message "another operation is running on this workspace; retry later"
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real carrypatch recovery hook with a real trunk and a stub fetch recording calls
   - setup: wslock held for the slug by another operation
   ```
   unlock = wslock.TryLock(slug); r = post(path); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.type == 'workspace_busy'; assert fetch.calls == 0; assert refs_before == refs_after
   ```
1. [REQ-2.8] IF no recovery hook is registered, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL reject the reset request
   → HTTP 500 with message "patch reset is not configured"
   Check: unit
   - setup: the recovery hook is nil
   ```
   RegisterRecoveryHook(nil); r = post(path); assert r.status == 500; assert r.json.error.message == 'patch reset is not configured'
   ```

### REQ-3: Reset semantics: fetch, compare and move

**Rationale:** The reset must act on the fork's current tip and discard hub commits only with a backup written first.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a reset holds the workspace lock, THE reset operation SHALL run the single-branch fetch +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch> with origin credentials (GIT_PAT, then GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD, then none) in both PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE modes, then resolve the fork tip as refs/remotes/origin/<branch>^{commit} and the local tip as refs/heads/<branch>^{commit} (possibly absent)
   → the fetch is called once per reset with refspec +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch>; credentials follow the order GIT_PAT, then username/password, then none; after the fetch the fork tip is read from refs/remotes/origin/<branch>^{commit} and the local tip from refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real bare fork and real trunk
   - setup: a stub fetch function recording refspec and credentials
   - setup: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE set to hub, then origin
   - setup: credentials in turn: GIT_PAT, GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD, none
   ```
   for mode in ['hub','origin']: for creds in cases: reset(); assert fetch.calls[-1].refspec == '+refs/heads/b:refs/remotes/origin/b'; assert fetch.calls[-1].auth == expected(creds)
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF origin credential resolution fails or the single-branch fetch fails for a reason other than a missing branch, THEN THE reset operation SHALL write no ref, log the underlying error text and not echo it
   → HTTP 502 with message "failed to resolve origin credentials" for a credential failure, or message "origin fetch failed" with error type origin_fetch_failed for a fetch failure; every ref is unchanged
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real trunk with a local branch and a backup ref
   - setup: a log capture
   - setup: a resolver failing with text "secret-token-xyz", and a fetch stub failing with text "dial tcp 10.0.0.1 refused"
   ```
   r = reset(cred_fail); assert r.status == 502 and r.msg == 'failed to resolve origin credentials'; r = reset(fetch_fail); assert r.json.error.type == 'origin_fetch_failed'; assert 'dial tcp' not in r.body; assert 'dial tcp' in logs; assert snapshot_refs() == before
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF the fork does not have the branch, THEN THE reset operation SHALL write no ref
   → HTTP 409 with error type missing_on_origin and message "branch does not exist on origin"; every ref is unchanged
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real bare fork lacking the patch branch
   - setup: a real trunk holding the branch and a backup ref
   - setup: the real single-branch fetch classification
   ```
   r = reset(); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.type == 'missing_on_origin'; assert r.msg == 'branch does not exist on origin'; assert snapshot_refs() == before
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] WHEN the local branch is missing, or the local and fork tips are the same commit, THE reset operation SHALL when missing, create refs/heads/<branch> at the fork tip with a compare-and-swap create and report action created; when the same commit, write nothing and report action none; write no backup in either case
   → HTTP 200 with action created or none; refs/hub/replaced/<branch> is unchanged
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real bare fork with the branch
   - setup: a real trunk once without the local branch and once with it at the fork tip
   - setup: an existing backup ref in the trunk
   ```
   r = reset(no_local); assert r.action == 'created'; assert rev('refs/heads/b') == fork_tip; r = reset(same); assert r.action == 'none'; assert rev(backup) == backup_before
   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] WHEN the local tip is a strict ancestor of the fork tip (GitRunner.IsAncestor on SHAs), THE reset operation SHALL move the local branch to the fork tip, report action fast_forwarded and leave any existing backup ref untouched
   → HTTP 200; refs/hub/replaced/<branch> keeps its previous value or stays absent
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real fork whose branch is ahead of the trunk's local branch by two commits
   - setup: an earlier backup ref pointing at an older discarded commit, and a second case with no backup
   ```
   r = reset(); assert r.action == 'fast_forwarded'; assert rev('refs/heads/b') == fork_tip; assert rev_or_none(backup) == backup_before
   ```
1. [REQ-3.6] WHEN the local tip and fork tip differ and the local tip is not a strict ancestor of the fork tip (diverged, or the fork tip is a strict ancestor of the local tip), THE reset operation SHALL write the local tip to refs/hub/replaced/<branch>, overwriting any earlier backup, then move the local branch to the fork tip and report action replaced
   → HTTP 200 with action replaced; replaced_sha equals the pre-reset local tip; a repeated replaced reset overwrites the backup
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real fork and trunk with diverged tips
   - setup: a second scenario where the fork tip is a strict ancestor of the local tip
   ```
   r1 = reset(); assert r1.action == 'replaced' and rev(backup) == local_before; commit_on_local(); r2 = reset(); assert rev(backup) == local_before2 != local_before
   ```
1. [REQ-3.7] THE reset operation SHALL for any branch move or creation, use the spec 20 compare-and-swap helper (update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>, never checkout, reset or branch -f) and hard-reset the working tree when the moved branch is the trunk's checked-out branch, so the working tree follows the branch
   → the branch write is `update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>` and no checkout, reset or branch -f command touches the patch branch; when the branch is checked out, HEAD, index and working tree equal the fork tip afterwards, with no dirty state; the branch ref equals the fork tip when the action is not none
   Check: property
   - setup: a real trunk and bare fork
   - setup: a git runner wrapper recording every command
   ```
   for g in gen_graphs(): setup(g); reset(); assert not any(c.args[0] in ('checkout','branch') for c in runner.cmds); if checked_out: assert git('status --porcelain') == '' and worktree_matches(fork_tip)
   ```
1. [REQ-3.8] IF the compare-and-swap write fails because the ref changed after the SHAs were resolved, or the write fails for any other reason, THEN THE reset operation SHALL abort the reset, keep any backup already written, and make no further ref writes
   → HTTP 409 with error type ref_changed and message "patch branch changed during reset; retry" for a lost race; HTTP 500 with message "failed to update patch branch <branch>" for any other failure
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real trunk and fork with diverged tips
   - setup: a hook point that makes a hub push move the local branch between SHA resolution and the write
   - setup: a second scenario where update-ref fails for another reason (read-only ref lock)
   ```
   r = reset(with_race); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.type == 'ref_changed'; assert rev(backup) == tip_read; r = reset(other_fail); assert r.status == 500 and r.msg == 'failed to update patch branch b'
   ```

### REQ-4: Reset: persisted sync state and rebuild trigger

**Rationale:** A branch moved by a reset looks in_sync at the next sync, so the reset must record state and trigger the rebuild itself.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHILE PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is origin, THE reset operation SHALL after a reset completes with any action, record the patch via the spec 20 PatchStore method as origin_sync_state in_sync with origin_sha set to the fork tip and origin_synced_at set to the current time
   → the patch row has origin_sync_state in_sync; origin_sha equals the fork tip; origin_synced_at is within a few seconds of now
   Check: integration
   - setup: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin
   - setup: a real PatchStore on a test database
   - setup: a patch with origin_sync_state diverged
   - setup: reset scenarios for created, none, fast_forwarded and replaced
   ```
   for action in actions: setup(action); reset(); row = store.get(patch); assert row.origin_sync_state == 'in_sync'; assert row.origin_sha == fork_tip; assert now - row.origin_synced_at < 5s
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHILE PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is hub, THE reset operation SHALL write no origin sync state
   → the origin-state PatchStore method is never called; origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at are unchanged
   Check: integration
   - setup: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=hub
   - setup: a patch row with null origin_* columns and a recording PatchStore
   ```
   reset(); assert store.origin_state_calls == 0; assert row_after == row_before
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN the reset action is created, fast_forwarded or replaced and the patch status is active or conflict and AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is not "false", THE reset operation SHALL enqueue a rebuild job with the same type, key slug, group slug:integration_branch, payload builder and deduplication as sync, with SubmittedBy set to the caller
   → response rebuild_triggered true and rebuild_job_id set to the new job id
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real job queue
   - setup: a patch with status active, then one with conflict
   - setup: AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC unset
   - setup: resets with action created, fast_forwarded and replaced
   ```
   r = reset(); job = queue.get(r.rebuild_job_id); assert job.type == 'rebuild' and job.key == slug and job.group == f'{slug}:{integration}'; assert job.submitted_by == caller; assert r.rebuild_triggered
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] WHILE AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is "false", THE reset operation SHALL enqueue no rebuild job after a branch move
   → response rebuild_triggered false and no rebuild_job_id
   Check: integration
   - setup: variable AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC set to "false"
   - setup: an active patch whose reset will replace the branch
   ```
   r = reset(); assert r.rebuild_triggered == False; assert 'rebuild_job_id' not in r; assert queue.count() == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] WHILE the patch status is disabled, THE reset operation SHALL move the branch but enqueue no rebuild job, because the rebuild skips disabled patches
   → response rebuild_triggered false and no rebuild_job_id
   Check: integration
   - setup: a disabled patch whose branch differs from the fork tip
   ```
   r = reset(disabled_patch); assert rev(branch) == fork_tip; assert queue.count() == 0; assert not r.rebuild_triggered
   ```
1. [REQ-4.6] WHEN the reset action is none, THE reset operation SHALL enqueue no rebuild job
   → HTTP 200 with rebuild_triggered false
   Check: integration
   - setup: local and fork tips identical
   - setup: an active patch
   ```
   r = reset(); assert r.status == 200 and r.action == 'none'; assert not r.rebuild_triggered; assert queue.count() == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-4.7] WHEN the rebuild enqueue is deduplicated by the job queue, THE reset operation SHALL leave rebuild_triggered false
   → HTTP 200 with rebuild_triggered false and no rebuild_job_id
   Check: integration
   - setup: an already queued rebuild job with the same key and group
   - setup: an active patch whose branch will move
   ```
   enqueue_rebuild(slug); r = reset(); assert r.status == 200 and not r.rebuild_triggered; assert 'rebuild_job_id' not in r; assert queue.count() == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-4.8] IF the rebuild enqueue returns an error, THEN THE reset operation SHALL log the error and complete the reset
   → HTTP 200 with rebuild_triggered false; the branch move stays in place
   Check: integration
   - setup: a job queue stub whose Enqueue returns an error
   - setup: an active patch whose branch will move
   ```
   r = reset(queue=failing); assert r.status == 200 and not r.rebuild_triggered; assert rev(branch) == fork_tip; assert logs.contains(ERROR_OR_WARN)
   ```

### REQ-5: CLI: afc patch reset-to-origin

**Rationale:** Operators drive recovery from the CLI, so the command must map directly to the endpoint.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN the operator runs afc patch reset-to-origin <workspace-slug> <patch-id>, THE afc CLI SHALL send POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/patches/<id>/reset-to-origin with no body and print the JSON result
   → exit code 0 and the response JSON printed to standard output
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub HTTP server answering 200 with a patch JSON including replaced_sha
   ```
   out, code = run(['patch','reset-to-origin','ws','7']); assert stub.method == 'POST' and stub.path == '/api/v1/workspaces/ws/patches/7/reset-to-origin'; assert stub.body == ''; assert code == 0; assert json(out) == response
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] IF the number of positional arguments is not exactly two, THEN THE afc CLI SHALL reject the invocation and send no request
   → non-zero exit code and no HTTP request made
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub HTTP server counting requests
   ```
   for args in [[], ['ws'], ['ws','1','x']]: code = run(['patch','reset-to-origin']+args); assert code != 0; assert stub.requests == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] IF the server answers with an error status, THEN THE afc CLI SHALL propagate the error through apikit.CLIHandleError with SilenceErrors and SilenceUsage set as for patch restore
   → non-zero exit code with the server error message reported
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub server answering 409 with message "patch status deleted cannot be reset"
   - setup: a second stub answering 502 origin fetch failed
   ```
   out, err, code = run(...); assert code != 0; assert 'cannot be reset' in err; assert 'Usage:' not in err+out; assert cmd.SilenceErrors and cmd.SilenceUsage
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] THE afc CLI SHALL state in the reset-to-origin help text the backup ref refs/hub/replaced/<branch> and the replaced_sha field, and add no flags including no --force
   → help contains "refs/hub/replaced/" and "replaced_sha"; the command defines no local flags and no --force flag
   Check: unit
   - setup: the constructed PatchCmd tree
   ```
   c = find(PatchCmd, 'reset-to-origin'); h = help(c); assert 'refs/hub/replaced/' in h and 'replaced_sha' in h; assert c.LocalFlags().lookup('force') is None; assert count(c.LocalNonPersistentFlags()) == 0
   ```

### REQ-6: Protect refs/hub/replaced/ in the git server

**Rationale:** Only the hub writes backup refs; a client that could overwrite them would destroy the recovery data.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN a client push creates, updates or deletes a ref whose name starts with refs/hub/replaced/, THE git server SHALL reject that ref at the spec 22 receive-pack interception point, before the registered pre-receive hook is consulted, and keep the ref's old value
   → client sees unpack ok and ng <ref> "refs/hub/replaced/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to"
   Check: integration
   - setup: a running git server over a real trunk with a git:write credential
   - setup: a pre-receive hook registered that would accept everything
   - setup: an existing refs/hub/replaced/feature ref
   ```
   out = git_push('+X:refs/hub/replaced/new'); assert 'ng refs/hub/replaced/new refs/hub/replaced/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to' in out; assert hook.calls == 0; assert rev(trunk, backup) == before
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] THE git server SHALL for any workspace, any workspace mode, any credential with git:write and any ref name starting with refs/hub/replaced/, reject the push of that ref, whether or not a pre-receive hook is registered
   → the ref is rejected with the protected-namespace message; the trunk ref is unchanged
   Check: property
   - setup: git servers over workspaces in standard and carry_patch modes
   - setup: with and without a registered pre-receive hook
   - setup: admin, api key and PAT credentials holding git:write
   ```
   for mode, hook, cred, name, op in product(modes, hooks, creds, gen_names('refs/hub/replaced/'), ops): out = push(op, name); assert rejected(out, name); assert trunk_ref(name) == before
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] WHEN a single push contains a refs/hub/replaced/ ref and the same push also contains a ref outside the protected namespace, THE git server SHALL process the other refs as usual and reject only the protected ref
   → the normal branch is written and the protected ref keeps its old value
   Check: integration
   - setup: a running git server over a real trunk
   - setup: an existing backup ref
   ```
   out = push(['X:refs/hub/replaced/feature','X:refs/heads/newbranch']); assert 'ok refs/heads/newbranch' in out and 'ng refs/hub/replaced/feature' in out; assert rev(trunk,'refs/heads/newbranch') == X; assert rev(trunk, backup) == before
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] WHEN a protected ref is rejected, THE git server SHALL trigger no head_sha update, no audit entry and no post-push hook for that ref
   → head_sha is unchanged; no audit entry is emitted; the post-push hook is not called
   Check: integration
   - setup: a git server wired with a recording head_sha updater, audit emitter and post-push hook
   - setup: a push containing only a protected ref
   ```
   push('X:refs/hub/replaced/f'); assert head_sha_updates == 0; assert audit.events == []; assert post_push.calls == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-6.5] THE git server SHALL for any ref name outside refs/hub/replaced/, including other names under refs/hub/, not apply the protected-namespace rule
   → the ref is accepted and written; the protected-namespace message never appears
   Check: property
   - setup: a git server over a real trunk with no pre-receive hook registered
   ```
   for name in gen_names_not_prefixed('refs/hub/replaced/'): out = push('X:'+name); assert 'ok '+name in out; assert 'maintained by the hub' not in out
   ```
1. [REQ-6.6] WHEN a client runs git ls-remote or git fetch <hub_url> refs/hub/replaced/<branch>, THE git server SHALL advertise the backup ref and serve its commit
   → ls-remote lists refs/hub/replaced/<branch> and the fetch succeeds with the backup commit
   Check: integration
   - setup: a running git server over a trunk holding refs/hub/replaced/feature at a commit not reachable from any branch
   ```
   assert (SHA+'\trefs/hub/replaced/feature') in git('ls-remote', url); git('fetch', url, 'refs/hub/replaced/feature'); assert git('rev-parse FETCH_HEAD') == SHA
   ```
1. [REQ-6.7] THE git server SHALL leave hub-internal writes to refs/hub/replaced/ (sync, reset, removal), which do not pass through a client push, unaffected by the rule
   → each internal write succeeds; a client fetch sees the value after each write
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real trunk served by the git server
   - setup: a hub-internal update-ref and a reset that writes a backup
   ```
   runner.UpdateRef(backup, A); assert fetch(backup) == A; runner.UpdateRef(backup, B); assert fetch(backup) == B; hook.RemoveBackup(slug, b); assert rev_or_none(backup) is None
   ```

### REQ-7: Backup cleanup on afc patch remove

**Rationale:** A removed patch must not leave an orphan backup ref behind, and a failed cleanup must not undo a completed delete.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN deletePatchAndCompact succeeds in handleRemovePatch and a recovery hook is registered, THE workspace handler SHALL ask the hook to delete refs/hub/replaced/<branch> (git update-ref -d), taking the branch name from the patch lookup made before deletion

   - setup: the real carrypatch recovery hook registered

1. [REQ-7.2] WHEN the backup ref does not exist at removal, THE recovery hook SHALL treat the removal as a success

   - setup: the real recovery hook

1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN the workspace trunk is not on disk at removal (for example an archived workspace), THE recovery hook SHALL treat the removal as a success and log it at info level

   Check: integration

   - setup: a log capture

1. [REQ-7.4] IF the hook fails to remove the ref for any other reason, THEN THE workspace handler SHALL log a warn entry with slug, branch and error and not change the response, because the row is already gone

   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hook whose RemoveBackup returns an error
   - setup: a log capture

1. [REQ-7.5] WHILE the workspace lock is held by a running sync, THE workspace handler SHALL remove the patch without taking the workspace lock
   → HTTP 204, never 409
   Check: integration
   - setup: wslock held for the slug by a simulated sync
   - setup: a backup ref in the trunk

1. [REQ-7.6] WHILE no recovery hook is registered, THE workspace handler SHALL remove no ref and remove the patch as before
   → HTTP 204
   Check: unit

1. [REQ-7.7] WHEN a patch is soft-deleted by a rebuild and later restored with POST .../restore, THE carry-patch operations SHALL leave refs/hub/replaced/<branch> untouched by the soft deletion so the restored patch keeps its backup
   → the backup ref has the same value before the soft deletion and after the restore
   Check: integration
   - setup: a patch with a backup ref pointing at SHA S


### REQ-8: Backup cleanup on purge of soft-deleted patches

**Rationale:** Purging rows without their refs would orphan the backups, and nothing else would find them.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] THE PatchStore SHALL provide a method that lists soft-deleted rows older than a cutoff with id, workspace slug and branch name, implemented by SQLPatchStore and by every test double
   → only the older soft-deleted rows are returned, each with id, workspace slug and branch name; active rows and newer deleted rows are excluded; all test doubles compile against the interface
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test database with soft-deleted rows older and newer than a cutoff, plus an active row
   - setup: every PatchStore test double compiled against the interface

1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN the ref-aware purge routine runs, THE purge routine SHALL for each expired soft-deleted row, remove refs/hub/replaced/<branch> in that workspace's trunk (using the workspace root and the carry-patch git runner factory) and then delete the row by id only while status='deleted', using a 7-day retention
   → returns the number of rows purged
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real database and workspace roots with trunks
   - setup: two expired soft-deleted rows, one with a backup ref and one without, in different workspaces
   - setup: the carry-patch git runner factory

1. [REQ-8.3] IF removing the backup ref of an expired row fails, THEN THE purge routine SHALL keep that row for the next purge, log a warn entry and continue with the remaining rows

   Check: integration
   - setup: three expired rows
   - setup: a runner factory whose update-ref -d fails for the second row's workspace
   - setup: a log capture

1. [REQ-8.4] WHEN the backup ref is missing or the workspace trunk is not on disk for an expired row, THE purge routine SHALL treat the ref removal as a success and delete the row
   → the row is deleted and counted
   Check: integration

   - setup: one expired row whose workspace trunk directory does not exist

   ```
   n = purge(); assert n == 2; assert rows_count() == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-8.5] WHEN a soft-deleted row is within the retention window, THE purge routine SHALL leave the row and its backup ref untouched
   → the 6-day-old row still exists with status deleted; its backup ref is unchanged; only the 8-day-old row is purged
   Check: integration

   → PurgeDeletedPatches keeps its signature and returns the deleted count; PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches(ctx, store) deletes expired rows with a 7-day cutoff; neither touches backup refs; the ref-aware routine is a separate function
   Check: unit

1. [REQ-8.7] IF listing the expired rows fails, THEN THE purge routine SHALL return the error and delete no row and no ref

### REQ-10: Audit events and logging

**Rationale:** Operators must be able to find every reset and every discarded commit in the audit log.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-10.1] WHEN a reset completes successfully, THE reset operation SHALL emit one hub.patch.reset event (constant added to internal/audit/types.go next to EventRebuildFollowup) with resource_type patch, the workspace slug, the caller as actor and metadata {branch_name, action, local_sha, origin_sha, replaced_sha}, where action is none, created, fast_forwarded or replaced
   → one hub.patch.reset audit entry per successful reset
   Check: integration
   - setup: a recording audit emitter
   - setup: the constant EventPatchReset in internal/audit/types.go
   - setup: reset scenarios for none, created, fast_forwarded and replaced
   ```
   ev = audit.events_of('hub.patch.reset'); assert len(ev) == 1; assert ev[0].resource_type == 'patch' and ev[0].actor == caller; assert ev[0].meta.action == expected and ev[0].meta.origin_sha == fork_tip
   ```
1. [REQ-10.2] THE reset operation SHALL for any hub.patch.reset event, omit local_sha when there was no local branch and include replaced_sha only when the action is replaced
   → local_sha key is absent exactly when there was no local branch; replaced_sha key is present exactly when action is replaced and equals the pre-reset local tip; action is one of the four allowed values
   Check: property
   - setup: a recording audit emitter
   ```
   for o in gen_outcomes(): m = emit(o).meta; assert ('local_sha' in m) == o.had_local; assert ('replaced_sha' in m) == (o.action == 'replaced'); assert m.action in ALLOWED
   ```
1. [REQ-10.3] WHEN a reset has action replaced, THE reset operation SHALL also emit hub.patch.replace with branch_name, replaced_sha, origin_sha and trigger set to reset_to_origin
   → a hub.patch.replace audit entry whose metadata trigger equals reset_to_origin
   Check: integration
   - setup: a recording audit emitter
   - setup: a diverged patch
   ```
   ev = audit.events_of('hub.patch.replace'); assert len(ev) == 1; assert ev[0].meta.trigger == 'reset_to_origin'; assert ev[0].meta.replaced_sha == local_before
   ```
1. [REQ-10.4] THE sync operation SHALL emit hub.patch.replace events with no trigger key, which consumers read as sync
   → a hub.patch.replace event is emitted; its metadata has no trigger key
   Check: integration
   - setup: a workspace with PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY set to replace and a diverged patch
   - setup: a recording audit emitter
   ```
   sync(); ev = audit.events_of('hub.patch.replace')[0]; assert 'trigger' not in ev.meta
   ```
1. [REQ-10.5] IF a reset fails with any error, THEN THE reset operation SHALL emit no audit event
   → zero hub.patch.reset and zero hub.patch.replace events recorded
   Check: integration
   - setup: a recording audit emitter
   - setup: failure scenarios: busy, credential failure, fetch failure, missing on origin, ref changed, update failure

   ```
   for s in failures: r = reset(s); assert r.status in (409,502,500); assert audit.events == []
   ```
1. [REQ-10.6] IF the audit emitter is nil or returns an error, THEN THE reset operation SHALL skip emission when nil, or log the error when it fails, without affecting the outcome

   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hook returning a replaced result
   - setup: emitter configurations: working, nil, returning an error
   - setup: a log capture

1. [REQ-10.7] WHEN a replacement (replaced reset) or a backup-ref removal occurs, THE reset operation SHALL log it at info level with slug, branch and the SHAs involved
   → an info entry for the replacement carries slug, branch, local SHA and origin SHA; an info entry for the removal carries slug, branch and the removed ref
   Check: integration
   - setup: a log capture

   ```
   reset(); e = logs.info(contains='replace'); assert e.slug and e.branch and e.replaced_sha and e.origin_sha; delete(path); assert logs.info(contains='backup').branch == b
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: Operator resets a diverged patch to the fork tip and the rebuild follows

1. **operator** runs afc patch reset-to-origin <slug> <patch-id> after a diverged report
2. **afc CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/patches/<id>/reset-to-origin with no body
3. **workspace handler** checks scope, ownership, workspace state, clone status and patch eligibility, then calls the recovery hook
4. **recovery hook** takes the workspace lock and fetches +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch> from the fork
5. **recovery hook** finds the tips diverged, writes the local tip to refs/hub/replaced/<branch> and moves refs/heads/<branch> to the fork tip with a compare-and-swap update-ref
6. **recovery hook** records in_sync origin state in origin mode and enqueues a rebuild job submitted by the caller
7. **workspace handler** emits hub.patch.reset and hub.patch.replace (trigger reset_to_origin) and returns 200 with the patch object, replaced_sha, rebuild_triggered and rebuild_job_id

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** afc CLI, HTTP server and workspace handlers, carrypatch recovery hook, git runner with real git, bare fork repository, trunk repository, job queue, audit store, database, wslock

**Setup:**

- a running hub with real handlers, real carrypatch hook, real database, real bare fork and trunk
- PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin
- a diverged active patch branch
- a real job queue and audit store

**End state:**

- the CLI exits 0 and prints the patch JSON with replaced_sha, rebuild_triggered true and rebuild_job_id
- the trunk branch equals the fork tip and refs/hub/replaced/<branch> equals the old local tip
- the patch row is in_sync with origin_sha set
- a rebuild job submitted by the caller is queued
- hub.patch.reset and hub.patch.replace (trigger reset_to_origin) audit entries exist

### PATH-2: Operator recovers a discarded tip from the backup ref

1. **operator** sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/patches/<id> for a patch whose branch was replaced
2. **workspace handler** reads refs/hub/replaced/<branch> through the recovery hook and returns the patch object with the 40-character replaced_sha
3. **operator** runs git fetch <hub_url> refs/hub/replaced/<branch>
4. **git server** advertises and serves the backup ref through git-upload-pack and the operator receives the discarded commit

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP server and workspace handlers, carrypatch recovery hook, git server (upload-pack via git CLI), trunk repository, real git client, database

**Setup:**

- a running hub with real git server, handlers and hook
- a patch whose branch was replaced so the trunk holds refs/hub/replaced/<branch>

**End state:**

- the GET returns replaced_sha with 40 hex characters
- the fetch succeeds
- the fetched commit equals replaced_sha

### PATH-3: A client push to the backup namespace is rejected while other refs are accepted

1. **client** pushes refs/hub/replaced/<branch> together with a normal branch to the hub git server
2. **git server** evaluates the fixed protected-namespace rule at the receive-pack interception point before the pre-receive hook
3. **git server** writes the normal branch, rejects the protected ref with ng <ref> refs/hub/replaced/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to, and keeps the old backup value
4. **client** receives unpack ok with one ng line and one accepted ref

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** git server receive-pack, trunk repository, real git client, auth middleware, database

**Setup:**

- a running hub git server with a real trunk and a git:write credential
- an existing refs/hub/replaced/<branch> backup

**End state:**

- the client sees unpack ok, one ng line with the protected-namespace message and one accepted ref
- refs/heads/newbranch exists in the trunk
- the backup keeps its old value

### PATH-4: Removing a patch removes its backup ref

1. **operator** runs afc patch remove for a patch that has a backup ref
2. **workspace handler** looks up the patch row, deletes it with deletePatchAndCompact and emits hub.patch.delete
3. **recovery hook** runs git update-ref -d refs/hub/replaced/<branch> in the workspace trunk without taking the workspace lock
4. **workspace handler** returns 204 and the backup ref no longer exists

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** afc CLI, HTTP server and workspace handlers, carrypatch recovery hook, git runner with real git, trunk repository, audit store, database

**Setup:**

- a running hub with real handlers, hook, database and trunk
- a patch with a backup ref

**End state:**

- the call succeeds with 204 semantics
- the patch row is gone and hub.patch.delete is emitted
- refs/hub/replaced/<branch> no longer exists in the trunk

### PATH-5: Purging expired soft-deleted patches removes their backup refs

1. **purge caller** invokes the ref-aware purge routine with the store, workspace root and git runner factory
2. **purge routine** lists soft-deleted rows older than 7 days with id, slug and branch
3. **purge routine** removes refs/hub/replaced/<branch> in each workspace trunk, treating a missing ref or trunk as success
4. **purge routine** deletes each row by id while status is deleted, keeps rows whose ref removal failed, and returns the purged count

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** purge routine, SQLPatchStore, git runner factory with real git, trunk repositories, database

**Setup:**

- a real database with expired and recent soft-deleted rows across two workspaces
- real trunks holding backup refs
- the carry-patch git runner factory

**End state:**

- expired rows and their backup refs are removed
- a row whose ref removal failed is kept
- recent rows remain with their refs
- the returned count equals the purged rows

### PATH-6: A reset that cannot reach the fork writes nothing

1. **operator** sends POST .../patches/<id>/reset-to-origin while the fork is unreachable
2. **recovery hook** takes the workspace lock, runs the single-branch fetch and receives a failure
3. **workspace handler** logs the error text, returns 502 origin fetch failed with error type origin_fetch_failed, and emits no audit event
4. **recovery hook** releases the workspace lock with every ref unchanged

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP server and workspace handlers, carrypatch recovery hook, real single-branch fetch, git runner with real git, trunk repository, audit store, wslock, database

**Setup:**

- a running hub with real handlers, hook and trunk
- a fork URL that refuses connections, using the real fetch
- a recording audit store

**End state:**

- the status is 502 with message "origin fetch failed" and error type origin_fetch_failed
- the response omits the underlying network error text
- every trunk ref is unchanged and no audit event is recorded
- the workspace lock is free afterwards


# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `make test`
- **linter:** `make lint`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/workspace/... ./internal/carrypatch/... ./internal/gitserver/... ./internal/cli/... ./internal/audit/... -count=1 -run 'TS23|Recovery|ResetToOrigin|ReplacedSHA|Purge|Protected'`

## Dependencies

- `01` — the rebuild job enqueued by a reset is executed by that spec's executor; its logic is unchanged
- `20` — provides refs/hub/replaced writes, PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE parser, compare-and-swap ref-move helper, PatchStore origin-state methods, origin credential resolver, the 502 messages and hub.patch.replace event
- `21` — provides the single-branch fork fetch, its missing-branch classification and the workspace/carrypatch hook pattern
- `22` — provides the receive-pack per-ref interception point and accepted-refs-only rule where the protected-namespace rule is added

### 3. Implement the carrypatch recovery hook: reset fetch, compare and compare-and-swap move (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3, REQ-9.3

**Depends on:** 1

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Write the listed tests with a real bare fork, real trunk and an injectable fetch stub; confirm they fail
- 3.2 Create internal/carrypatch/recovery.go: a RecoveryService constructed with the git runner factory, workspace root, variable getter (store.GetVariableValue), spec 20 origin credential resolver, an injectable single-branch fetch func (default: spec 21 fetch), job queue, spec 20 PatchStore methods and PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE parser; expose ReadReplacedSHA, RemoveBackup and RunReset
- 3.3 ReadReplacedSHA: runner rev-parse --verify --end-of-options refs/hub/replaced/<branch>^{commit}; absent ref -> not found; missing trunk dir -> not found without error
- 3.4 RemoveBackup: git update-ref -d refs/hub/replaced/<branch>; missing ref is success; missing trunk is success with slog.Info; other errors returned (shared helper also used by purge)
- 3.5 RunReset: wslock.TryLock(slug) only inside the hook (busy -> classified Busy error); fetch +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch> in both modes with credentials via the resolver (credential failure / fetch failure / missing branch classified, underlying text logged not returned); no ref writes on these failures
- 3.6 Resolve fork tip refs/remotes/origin/<branch>^{commit} and local tip refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}; apply first matching rule: missing local -> CAS create (action created); same SHA -> none; local strict ancestor of fork (GitRunner.IsAncestor on SHAs) -> fast_forwarded, no backup; else write backup with GitRunner.UpdateRef then move (action replaced)
- 3.7 Move through spec 20's compare-and-swap helper (update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>, hard reset of worktree when branch is checked out); if it is not callable from carrypatch, extract and share it rather than duplicate; lost race -> RefChanged, other failure -> Other, keep backup already written, no further writes
- 3.8 Define carrypatch-local result and error types (no import of workspace); in cmd/af-hub/main.go add an adapter that converts them to the workspace ResetResult/ResetError types and calls workspace.RegisterRecoveryHook next to the existing hook registrations
- 3.9 Confirm go list -deps shows no import between internal/workspace and internal/carrypatch in either direction
